title: Reproducible Performance Evaluation of OpenMP and SYCL Workloads under Noise Injection
problem: System noise (OS jitter, shared cache interference, NUMA effects) causes unpredictable performance variability in parallel computing. Existing evaluation methods cannot systematically characterize and mitigate noise effects on different parallel programming models.
motivation: OpenMP and SYCL are competing parallel programming models for HPC. Understanding their noise resilience is critical for workload optimization and system tuning, but reproducible noise characterization methodology is lacking.
method: The framework captures real system traces—the actual OS interrupts, cache contention, and memory access delays that happen in production—and replays them as controlled disturbances to test how different parallel programming models (OpenMP and SYCL) perform under stress. They evaluated each workload both with normal system behavior and with injected noise, trying three mitigation tactics: thread pinning (locking threads to specific processor cores), dedicating certain cores to housekeeping tasks only, and toggling SMT (simultaneous multithreading, where one core runs multiple threads) on or off. They measured performance using two standard benchmarks—N-body and Babelstream—plus a smaller test application called MiniFE. Testing happened on two different processor platforms to see how resilience varied across hardware.
key_novelty: This is the first systematic, reproducible method for measuring how well parallel programming models maintain performance when faced with controlled system noise injection.
contributions: Reproducible noise injection framework capturing real system traces
Systematic evaluation of OpenMP vs SYCL under noise
Comparative analysis of mitigation strategies (pinning, isolation, SMT)
Demonstration that SYCL exhibits greater noise resilience than OpenMP
Correlation between mitigation and workload characteristics
hardware_target: two processor platforms (specific architecture not named)

metrics.performance_variability: OpenMP higher raw, SYCL more resilient
metrics.mitigation_effectiveness: varies by workload and noise intensity

limitations: Evaluation limited to two processor platforms; specific architecture details not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Performance stability and reproducibility in parallel systems
